records.abstract: Non-uniform temperature distribution within mass concrete structures can lead to thermal cracking and then degrade durability. In order to accurately predict the temperature distribution, it is important to estimate the heat generation model that can quantitatively describe the exothermic behavior due to the hydration reaction of cement. In this study, physics-informed neural network was developed to characterize the heat generation and simultaneously predict the temperature distribution using only observed temperature data. By comparing the results obtained from numerical simulation based on representative empirical heat generation models with those obtained through inverse modeling using the neural network the effectiveness in characterizing the thermal behavior and predicting the temperature field in mass concrete structures was verified. To evaluate the robustness in solving the inverse problems, noise was added to the numerical simulation data, which was then used as the observed data. Upon successful training, the physics-informed neural network not only reconstructed the reference heat generation model employed in the numerical simulation with high fidelity, but also accurately predicted the temperature distribution beyond the spatial domain used for training. These results demonstrate the potential as a powerful tool for solving inverse problems of mass concrete heat analysis.

records.abstract: A physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PI-GPR) model for predicting the probabilistic flexural strength of corroded reinforced concrete (RC) columns was developed based on the multi-level embedding strategy. According to the moment equilibrium conditions, a physical model representing the flexural mechanism of corroded RC columns was established first. Subsequently, the multi-level embedding strategy was adopted to develop the PI-GPR model by constraining the mean, kernel, and loss functions hierarchically. Meanwhile, an adaptive trade-off between physical priors and data features was achieved by adding the dynamic coefficients that are continuously updated as training data changes. Then the PI-GPR model was applied to predict the probabilistic flexural strength of corroded RC columns. Finally, the effectiveness of the PI-GPR model was validated by comparing it with traditional prediction methods. Analysis results show that the PI-GPR model, which integrates the physical constraints with data-driven learning, demonstrates excellent performance and robust uncertainty quantification. Compared with traditional GPR, the PI-GPR ensures high physical consistency of predictions, which not only achieves an average improvement of 20% in confidence interval coverage when the training set proportion was only 30%, but also reduces the mean absolute error and root mean square error for edge samples by 23% and 21%, respectively.

records.abstract: Dams play a critical role in hydroelectric power generation, a strategic and renewable energy source. However, their potential for collapse poses significant risks, including environmental damage and loss of life. Ensuring dam safety, especially under seismic loading, requires detailed analysis of the interaction between structure, fluid, and foundation soil. This study proposes an integrated approach using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to assess the seismic stability of gravity dams. A finite element model was developed for a dam-reservoir-foundation system, incorporating spatial variability in the concrete’s elastic modulus through a stochastic simulation based on a continuous random field with a normalized correlation length of 0.10. The simulation results were used to train decision tree-based ML algorithms. Among them, the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model exhibited the highest predictive performance, achieving a correlation coefficient of 92.64 % on the test set. XGBoost was employed to estimate displacements and tensile stresses at critical locations, such as the neck and heel of the dam, where the maximum stress reached 9.36 MPa. Validation with additional simulations demonstrated prediction errors below 6.61 %, indicating strong agreement with the finite element results. This approach contributes to risk identification and supports more effective maintenance and safety management of dam infrastructure.

records.abstract: Existing physics-informed neural network frameworks for structural mechanics are often tied to a single geometric configuration, so changes in geometry require repeated model construction and retraining. This study develops a geometry-aware energy-based physics-informed neural network for Kirchhoff-Love plate bending over prescribed families of parameterized geometries. The main novelty of this work lies in the integration of geometric descriptors, hard boundary-satisfying trial functions, and a total potential energy functional based on the principle of minimum potential energy, thereby enabling a single model to learn the mapping from spatial coordinates and geometric parameters to structural responses within a prescribed admissible geometry family. This design enables one trained model to predict deformation fields for continuously varying geometries within a predefined admissible parameter domain while retaining a single-objective energy loss. Numerical experiments are conducted for aspect-ratio, internal-boundary, and joint-parameterization cases. Results show that the average deflection error is below 1% in the aspect-ratio case and remains within 3% in high-dimensional parameterization cases involving internal boundaries. These results indicate that, within predefined geometry families, the geometry-aware hard-constrained energy formulation can serve as a practical parametric modeling tool for repeated geometry evaluation, structural optimization and digital-twin applications.

records.abstract: As a structural system with high redundancy, optimizing cable-stayed bridges has always been a challenge. Traditional finite element modelling (FEM)-based simulation and optimization techniques are limited by repetitive model updating and computation. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN), emerged as a promising alternative to FEM, have been successfully used in numerical simulation or optimization tasks. However, existing research mainly focused on applying PINN to meso-scale numerical simulations of homogeneous material components, with limited exploration in structural-level analysis. The present study pioneers the application of PINN in integrated numerical simulation and optimization of cable-stayed bridges, a representative civil engineering structure. PINN surrogate models driven purely by physical equations are constructed and trained, achieving a high-precision mapping from any combination of values within the structural parameter design space to the corresponding structural static/dynamic responses. Leveraging the real-time simulation output capability of the well-trained PINN surrogate models, the efficiency of structural parameter optimization has been significantly improved. Comparisons with the current state-of-the-art FEM tool show that the proposed PINN method exhibits superior performance in both simulation and optimization tasks.

records.abstract: The rapid and accurate characterization of band structures is a fundamental challenge in the study of Phononic Crystals (PnCs), traditionally constrained by the high computational cost of numerical simulations. While deep learning surrogates offer significant acceleration, prevailing approaches predominantly rely on pixelated representations, which inherently compromise geometric fidelity and induce aliasing artifacts. To address this resolution bottleneck, we introduce the Hybrid Fourier Neural Operator (Hybrid FNO), a mesh-independent framework tailored for high-precision eigenfrequency prediction. Distinguishing itself from conventional image-based models, our architecture features a decoupled design that synergistically processes discrete scatterer boundaries via a spectral operator and explicitly integrates wave vectors through a parametric branch. This approach achieves two critical physical alignments: first, it exploits the resolution-invariance of FNOs to circumvent discretization errors; second, it mirrors the input–output structure of Finite Element solvers by treating the wave vector as an independent physical variable, thereby enabling robust cross-wave-vector generalization. By establishing a differentiable, physics-consistent mapping between complex topology and spectral properties, this study demonstrates a robust methodology for the efficient analysis of acoustic and elastic metamaterials without sacrificing precision.

records.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in energy form, also known as the deep energy method (DEM), offer advantages over strong form of PINNs such as lower-order derivatives and fewer hyperparameters, yet dedicated and user-friendly software for energy form of PINNs remains scarce. To address this gap, we present LM-DEM (Large Language Model-assisted Deep Energy Method), an open-source, Streamlit-based platform for solving variational partial differential equations (PDEs) in computational mechanics. LM-DEM integrates large language models (LLMs) for geometry modeling: users can generate Gmsh-compatible geometries directly from natural language descriptions or images, significantly reducing the burden of traditional geometry preprocessing. The solution process is driven by the deep energy method, while finite element solutions can be obtained in parallel. The framework supports built-in problems including Poisson, screened Poisson, linear elasticity, and hyperelasticity in two and three dimensions, as well as user-defined energy functionals analogous to the UMAT interface in Abaqus. The source code is available at https://github.com/yizheng-wang/LMDEM, and a web-based version is accessible at https://ai4m.llmdem.com. LM-DEM aims to lower the barrier for practitioners and beginners to adopt energy form of PINNs for variational PDE problems.

records.abstract: Accurate prediction of geometrically nonlinear bending in laminated composite plates remains a computational challenge in structural engineering. This paper presents a physics-informed neural network framework as a mesh-free approach to this problem. The methodology integrates Reddy’s higher-order shear deformation theory and von Kármán’s geometric nonlinearity to evaluate thick composites without relying on shear correction factors. To overcome the severe gradient pathologies and computational instability associated with the fourth-order spatial derivatives required by the strong-form governing equations, the loss function is formulated directly from the variational principle of minimum total potential energy. This energy-based objective reduces the required derivative order to the second degree, creating a mathematically stable optimization landscape that guides the network toward kinematically admissible equilibrium states. Furthermore, the neural network architecture and training hyperparameters are systematically evaluated using an automated hyperparameter optimization framework. The proposed framework was validated against established three-dimensional elasticity and finite element solutions, demonstrating consistent accuracy in capturing nonlinear responses and through-thickness stress distributions across diverse loading scenarios, boundary conditions, and laminate configurations. This article establishes a stable and data-efficient computational framework for the nonlinear analysis of laminated composite structures.

records.abstract: Coral aggregate concrete is a potential alternative to natural aggregate concrete for coastal building structures. Given that coastal structures often experience triaxial stress states, conventional empirical models rely on extensive experimental data, and their limited physical interpretability can hinder reliable prediction of coral aggregate concrete behavior when data are sparse. This study proposes a physics-informed neural networks framework embedding the unified five-parameter or modified unified twin-shear strength theory failure criteria, modified Guo’s piecewise constitutive model, and geometric boundary constraints to enable parameter inversion and stress–strain reconstruction. Conventional triaxial compression tests were conducted on coral aggregate concrete across varying strength grades, coral aggregate replacement rates, and confining pressure ratios. Experimental results show that higher confinement shifts failure from axial splitting to ductile oblique shear, increases peak stress, and alleviates post peak softening. Meanwhile, increased coral aggregate replacement rates intensify structural crushing. The developed framework accurately predicts multiaxial peak stress and reconstructs full stress-strain curves from sparse data. Validations demonstrate excellent predictive accuracy, achieving determination coefficients exceeding 0.97 and mean absolute percentage errors below 5 %. The framework maintains robust accuracy under 20 % data noise. This study provides an efficient and interpretable computational approach for characterizing the nonlinear mechanics of emerging engineering materials.

records.abstract: A dynamic response analysis method for parametric frame structures based on modal reduction basis predicted by physics-informed graph neural networks is proposed. A framework creating prediction model for modal reduction basis of parametric frame structures, which integrates graph neural networks with physical principles, using graph presentation as input is presented. The modal reduction basis prediction models of a damaged spatial truss and a frame structure are created by the proposed method and used to calculate the dynamic responses of the two structures with different damage indexes under dynamic loads. The prediction models can quickly and accurately determine the modal reduction bases of the structures during parameter evolution. In addition, the influences of network architectures including message passing graph neural network, graph convolutional network and graph attention network, and hyperparameters on the performance of modal reduction basis prediction models for parametric structures are analyzed. It is demonstrated that message passing graph neural network and graph convolutional network have superior ability to capture complex structural features and behavior. The presented creation method for modal reduction basis is efficient for quick analysis of dynamic response of parametric structures.

records.abstract: In this study, a data-driven approach is proposed to predict the damage gauge factor of self-sensing high-performance fiber-reinforced cementitious composites. A Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) was employed to expand a limited dataset of 86 samples, enabling robust model development. A hybrid Random Forest–Bayesian optimization model was then trained using combined real and synthetic data. The proposed approach achieved high predictive performance, with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.871, 0.863, and 0.863 for the training, testing, and 10-fold cross-validation stages, respectively, at an optimal 80/20 train–test split. SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) and Partial Dependence Plot analyses indicated that the matrix compressive strength, fiber aspect ratio, and change in electrical resistivity are key variables influencing the damage gauge factor. Moreover, a novel theoretical equation based on shapley value for predicting the damage gauge factor was derived demonstrating satisfactory performance. Finally, a user-friendly web-based application was developed to facilitate practical implementation. The proposed framework provides both accurate prediction and physical insight, offering a reliable and accessible tool for the design and structural health monitoring of self-sensing cementitious composites.

records.abstract: Large-span spatial structures are widely used in critical public facilities, but conventional incremental dynamic analysis (IDA)-based seismic fragility assessment is computationally intensive. This study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework to improve efficiency and interpretability. An IDA-based database was developed for three representative systems: a spherical reticulated shell, a cylindrical reticulated shell, and a flat grid structure. The framework integrates normalized time-domain waveforms, frequency-domain spectrograms, and physical intensity measures through a multi-branch fusion architecture. A two-stage classification–regression strategy and quantity-weighted loss are adopted to address imbalanced damage-state distributions. Fragility predictions are evaluated using the median parameter θ, logarithmic dispersion β, percentage errors, and curve agreement. With 40% of the dataset (480 samples), the multimodal feature model achieves R^{2} values of 0.9116, 0.8990, and 0.8757 for the three structures, with average θ and β errors of 6.41% and 20.81%, respectively. Increasing the training proportion to 80% further improves accuracy and highlights the benefit of multimodal fusion. SHAP analysis identifies physical measures, particularly Sa(T_{1}), as the dominant contributors, while time- and frequency-domain features provide complementary information. Compared with full IDA, the proposed framework reduces computational time by approximately 59.98% while maintaining acceptable accuracy.

records.abstract: The integration of neural network–based methods into scientific modeling has opened new opportunities for tackling complex challenges in constitutive modeling within computational mechanics. In practical settings, however, challenges arise due to the privacy constraints, distributed nature of data, and the difficulty of transferring large datasets. Federated learning offers an effective solution by enabling decentralized training of a global model while keeping data localized. In this work, we present, for the first time, a physics-guided Federated Scientific Machine Learning (FedSciML) framework for both inverse parameter identification of a constitutive model and direct approximation of polycarbonate material behavior under heterogeneous and decentralized data conditions. To systematically study data heterogeneity, we introduce controlled data generation strategies that produce non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) datasets and employ the 1-Wasserstein distance to quantify distributional differences. We further examine how varying the number of participating clients influences the level of heterogeneity. The results show that the proposed FedSciML framework effectively calibrates the constitutive model by identifying a unified parameter set that accurately reproduces experimental observations. In addition, the framework demonstrates strong predictive capability in learning material behavior even under severe data scarcity and highly non-IID conditions. Overall, both the global federated model and the local client models achieve accurate extrapolation across unseen regimes, without requiring direct data sharing. This highlights the robustness and practical relevance of the proposed approach.

records.abstract: Modeling plate bending responses under varying loads and boundary conditions remains challenging because of the high-order governing equation and boundary-dependent solution behavior. This study proposes a Boundary-Feature-Embedded Physics-Informed Deep Operator Network (BPI-DeepONet) for parametric Kirchhoff plate bending problems. The proposed framework encodes load functions through fixed Branch sensor values and represents boundary conditions using a learnable boundary embedding module. A nonlinear Branch–Trunk fusion network is introduced to enhance feature interaction, while an output transformation strongly enforces essential displacement boundary conditions. The governing equation and derivative-type boundary constraints are incorporated through physics-informed losses. Numerical assessments are conducted in a progressive manner. First, under fixed boundary conditions, the model demonstrates high accuracy for deterministic loads (uniform and sinusoidal loads with relative ${L}_{2}$ errors of 2.99% and 1.48%, respectively), Gaussian random field (GRF) loads, and GRF perturbations superimposed on background loads. Second, in the same-load multi-boundary benchmark, BPI-DeepONet effectively distinguishes boundary-dependent responses associated with identical load inputs, achieving a mean relative ${L}_{2}$ error of 2.81% $\pm $ 0.15%. Systematic ablation studies confirm that hard boundary enforcement is crucial for optimization stability, while nonlinear feature fusion significantly outperforms capacity-matched baselines.

records.abstract: Accurate characterization of the time-domain nonlinear mechanical behavior of viscoelastic dampers (VEDs) remains challenging. Traditional frequency-domain models cannot simultaneously consider loading history, strain amplitude, and ambient temperature, whereas high-fidelity time-domain models generally require complex parameter calibration and incur high computational cost. To overcome such limitations, a physics-guided convolutional neural network (CNN) surrogate model is proposed by integrating a one-dimensional CNN (1D CNN) within an equivalent linear viscoelasticity (ELV) model. A dual-branch CNN is subsequently developed to identify the ELV parameters, while the ELV model provides physical guidance through the loss function, resulting in an interpretable physics-data-driven framework. By leveraging available numerical and experimental data, the proposed model is validated from two representative energy dissipation devices (EDDs), demonstrating its ability to characterize nonlinear mechanical behavior and energy dissipation. Furthermore, the proposed model is applied to nonlinear dynamic analyses of viscoelastically damped frames under various earthquake excitations and ambient temperatures. The results show that the proposed model can accurately characterize the time-domain nonlinear mechanical behavior of two type of common EDDs, while its theoretical framework shows potential for extension to other damping devices. Structural dynamic analyses further indicate that neglecting viscoelastic nonlinearity may lead to inaccurate estimation of the energy-dissipation capacity of VEDs and introduce errors in seismic response evaluation. Moreover, ambient temperature may have a non-negligible influence on structural responses, predictions based on the nominal design temperature may deviate from the actual behavior under substantial temperature variations, which should be considered in engineering design.

records.abstract: This paper presents a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework based on the kinematic upper-bound formulation for rigid-perfectly plastic Mindlin plates. While PINNs have been increasingly adopted in computational mechanics, their capability to directly minimize the non-smooth plastic dissipation functional for evaluating structural collapse mechanisms has remained largely unexplored. By recasting limit analysis as a sampling-based neural variational optimization problem over admissible velocity fields, the proposed approach provides a mesh-free alternative to traditional finite element and second-order cone programming (SOCP) techniques. In this sampling-based variational framework, the transverse velocity and two independent rotation fields are approximated by neural networks, including both standard multilayer perceptrons and residual networks enriched with learnable Fourier feature embeddings. The von Mises plastic dissipation functional is integrated through the plate thickness by Gauss–Legendre quadrature and over the mid-plane by quasi-Monte Carlo integration, and is minimized subject to a unit external-work normalization. Essential kinematic boundary conditions are embedded through geometry-dependent hard constraints implemented by analytical masking functions and local projection operators. The unit-work condition is treated through work-normalization strategies, with penalty enforcement and explicit work normalization compared in the numerical study. Numerical studies are conducted for square, skew rhombic, circular, triangular, and hexagonal plates under clamped and simply supported boundary conditions. The results show that the proposed PINN formulation can reproduce the main collapse-load trends and dissipation patterns reported in reference upper-bound solutions, while the Fourier-enriched architecture generally improves the resolution of localized plastic dissipation. Furthermore, the thickness studies demonstrate that the continuous neural representation naturally mitigates the severe shear-locking phenomenon commonly associated with low-order Mindlin finite elements, maintaining robust collapse-load predictions even in the thin-plate limit. Finally, remaining sensitivities to network architecture, optimization effort, and geometric boundary treatments are identified and discussed.
